concerns.text: Human annotation is restricted to the top/bottom [deferred] drift bins, but FR-009 (logistic regression, AUC-ROC) and FR-010 (Flan-T5 AUC) are evaluated on this annotated set. Range restriction to the extremes of drift_score biases the regression coefficient, AUC, and Cohen's d (separation of extremes is near-guaranteed by construction). Either annotate a random sample of the full drift range, or restrict AUC/comparison claims to the binned subset and state the limitation.

Three annotators label 'novel attack'/'known attack'/'benign', but the spec never defines how the three-way labels are aggregated into the binary 'novel' gold standard used by FR-008/FR-009/FR-010 (majority vote? unanimity? how are 'known attack' logs treated — excluded or folded into benign?). The gold-standard construction rule must be specified, since it determines every downstream statistic.

Cohen's d ≥ 0.5 is paired with a Mann-Whitney U test. Cohen's d assumes approximately normal distributions; with a nonparametric test a rank-based effect size (e.g., rank-biserial or Cliff's delta) is more consistent. Specify which effect size and how d is computed (pooled SD) if retained.

The review_flag threshold drift_score ≥ 0.5 is asserted with no calibration rationale (cosine-distance scale depends on embedding geometry). State that it is a pre-registered operating point, or tie it to a quantile of the score distribution, so it is not confused with a validated decision boundary.
